title: Memory Safety Grid Orchestrator for Weights/KV/Activations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As continuous batching and KV cache use scale across multi-tenant GPUs, we hit transient OOMs and unpredictable tail latency when activations spike or KV working sets grow. Existing reserve-ledger approaches are effective but coarse; they either over-reserve (wasted capacity) or react too late (OOMs).

This ticket proposes a Memory Safety Grid Orchestrator: a runtime component that reasons about GPU memory as a 2D/3D safety grid across three axes (weights static footprint per model variant, KV cache dynamic occupancy per tenant/workload, and activation working sets by sequence-length/beam). The orchestrator provides fine-grained, probabilistic headroom recommendations, live occupancy signals, and preemptive mitigation actions (soft-preempt, spill-to-host, quantized variant fallback) to meet SLOs with minimal wasted capacity.
proposal:
High-level plan:
1) Telemetry & heatmaps: extend runtime telemetry to emit per-device, per-queue live occupancy heatmaps for weights, KV, and activations with 1s/5s aggregation windows.
2) Safety Grid Model: compute per-tenant grid cells with probabilistic occupancy distributions (recent window + decay), producing a per-cell headroom recommendation (soft reserve band).
3) Priority scoring: score active requests by SLA, tenant tier, and recent error-rate to decide eviction/preempt order when grid stress is detected.
4) Mitigations: implement a staged mitigation pipeline - (a) drop batching window (flush), (b) spill lower-priority KV shards to SSD or host memory, (c) switch new requests to quantized/model-variant with lower weight footprint, (d) last-resort soft-preempt (checkpoint KV for reconnect).
5) Simulation & safety checks: integrate with memory-sim harness to run production trace replays and validate no-OOM target for 99.9% of trace windows while measuring wasted reserved bytes.
6) Rollout: Canary on a small Dedicated pool, metric-backed gradual ramp tied to rollouts in Console.

Engineering components:
- telemetry schema changes (proto) and consumption path in agent;
- grid estimator service in runtime;
- eviction/preempt controller integrated with KV manager and batching scheduler;
- console dashboard panels (heatmap + recommended reserve bands).

Non-goals: full tenant-level hard partitioning, global scheduler changes outside device-local decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Telemetry: live occupancy heatmaps available for each device with <=2s delay.
- Simulator: run 30-day production trace replay; observed OOMs reduced to 0 for 99.9% of 1-minute windows compared to baseline.
- Latency/regression: p95 generation latency increase <=5% under normal load; mitigation steps are applied in <150ms after threshold crossing.
- Cost/regression: wasted reserved bytes across fleet reduced by >=15% versus static reserve policy.
- GA readiness: canary shows lower incident rate on Dedicated pool and no customer-facing errors.
- Docs: design doc + runbook published and linked in ticket.
rollout_plan:
1) Internal integration test with sim harness (dev env).
2) Canary on 2 Dedicated clusters with opt-in flag (1 week).
3) Expand to low-traffic production clusters with metric gates (2-3 weeks).
4) Full rollout to Dedicated after release gating and operator training.
Gates: OOM reduction, latency delta, and wasted-reserve improvements must meet targets before each stage.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives trigger unnecessary preemption -> Mitigation: require two-window confirmation and prioritize lower-impact mitigations first (flush batching).
Risk: KV spill performance regressions -> Mitigation: segment spill to HOT/Cold tiers and fallback to host-memory only for low-priority shards.
Risk: Telemetry volume and cost -> Mitigation: coarse-grain aggregation windows + sampling for low-traffic devices.
